report.headline: Riyadh halted since 9:29 PM Sunday, 2,790 minutes at 8:00 PM; NOTAM closes it until 12:00 AM Sunday 18 Oct. Erdoğan, Merz and Lebanon's president affirm solidarity against Houthi attacks
report.synopsis: Riyadh remains halted since 9:29 PM Sunday (2,730 minutes at 7:00 PM), with no takeoff or landing; NOTAM A3604/26 keeps the airport closed until 12:00 AM Sunday 18 Oct. The Cabinet, chaired by the Crown Prince, said the Houthis will bear the consequences of attacks on Saudi airports and the holy cities, praised Coalition operations in Yemen and said East-West pipeline crude flows have been restored. Explosions and strikes were reported in Sanaa and Ras Issa (not confirmed by the Coalition). Yesterday, 9 October: 166 of 703 flights cancelled, 18 arrivals diverted and four halts of 45+ minutes, the longest 7:41 to 9:38 PM (no landing until 9:45 PM). No official reason has been given for the evening stop. Saturday morning: a 91-minute halt ran from 6:37 to 8:08 AM with no takeoff or landing. Saturday afternoon–evening: the board showed no takeoff or landing from 2:05 PM until flynas XY278 from Sharm el-Sheikh landed at 8:10 PM (~365 minutes). Since that landing there has been no further takeoff or landing — open halt since 8:10 PM (470 minutes at the 4:00 AM Sunday slot). Last takeoff remains flynas XY277 at 1:39 PM; prior last landing before XY278 was Air Cairo SM461 at 2:05 PM. GACA confirms King Khalid International Airport was attacked on Saturday afternoon and operations remain temporarily suspended until damage assessment and facility safety checks are complete. GACA follow-up statement at 12:46 AM Sunday (dated 11 October): the attack resulted in 12 fatalities — 4 Saudi citizens and residents of Bangladeshi (2), American (1), Egyptian (1), Jordanian (1), Syrian (1), Palestinian (1) and Sudanese (1) nationality — and 309 injured, including some in critical condition; property damage is being assessed. AIS/NOTAC shows NOTAM A3586/26 (NOTAMR) keeping the aerodrome unavailable from 10 Oct 19:24 UTC through 11 Oct 21:00 UTC. Flightradar24 at 11:35 PM reported Dammam-bound flights holding (including one originally for Riyadh); at 12:01 AM FR24 said flights were on approach to Dammam again. Reuters at 9:40 PM had restated the suspension with “several” wounded — GACA’s 12:46 AM tally supersedes that on casualties. AP reports an official saying a missile struck a passenger terminal and wounded many; AFP hospital source earlier said dozens injured / at least five Saudis in ICU; AFP diplomatic source said Houthis hit with a missile around 3:00 PM. Social-media death-toll claims circulating earlier remain unverified against the new official GACA figures. No official Houthi claim for Saturday found yet. Passengers told to confirm flight status before heading to the airport. Board cancellations remain elevated on Sunday 11 October.

items.body: Libyan House of Representatives condemns the targeting of King Khalid International Airport in the Kingdom.

items.title: UK Minister of State for the Middle East phones Saudi deputy foreign minister to condemn Houthi terrorist attacks on the Kingdom and affirm UK support
items.body: Saudi deputy foreign minister received a call from the UK Minister of State for the Middle East condemning Houthi terrorist attacks on the Kingdom and affirming British support and solidarity.

items.title: Crown Prince receives call from Turkish President Erdoğan affirming full solidarity against Houthi attacks
items.body: HRH the Crown Prince receives a phone call from Turkish President; Erdoğan affirms full solidarity with Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks.

items.title: Crown Prince receives call from German Chancellor Merz affirming solidarity and condemning Houthi attacks
items.body: HRH the Crown Prince receives a phone call from German Chancellor; Merz affirms solidarity with Saudi Arabia and condemns Houthi attacks.

items.title: Crown Prince receives call from Lebanese President condemning attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.body: HRH the Crown Prince receives a phone call from Lebanese President condemning attacks on Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Yemeni media ministry adviser: airstrike hit As-Sabaha fuel station west of Sanaa used for Houthi military operations, with Houthi casualties reported
items.body: Yemeni Minister of Information adviser Dr. Aref Abu Hatim: reports that As-Sabaha station west of Sanaa, which holds central fuel tanks used for Houthi military operations, was struck, with Houthi casualties.

items.title: Cabinet: the Houthis will bear the consequences of attacks on the Kingdom's airports, Makkah and Madinah; Kingdom will not allow threats to Red Sea navigation
items.body: The Cabinet, chaired by the Crown Prince in Riyadh, said the Houthi militia will bear the consequences of its repeated attacks on Saudi airports, Makkah, Madinah, pilgrims and civilian and economic facilities, and praised the Coalition's military operations in Yemen. It said the Kingdom will not allow threats to its security or to freedom of navigation in the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, and commended national teams for restoring crude oil flows through the East-West pipeline.

items.title: Iranian navy says an oil tanker was damaged and caught fire in a “restricted zone” of the Strait of Hormuz
items.body: Al Jazeera, citing the Iranian navy, said an oil tanker sustained damage and caught fire while trying to pass through a restricted zone in the Strait of Hormuz with its tracking systems off. The vessel and cause have not been independently confirmed.

items.title: Al Jazeera sources: air strikes hit the Ras Issa port and oil area in Hodeidah
items.body: Sources in Yemen told Al Jazeera that air strikes hit the Ras Issa area of Hodeidah province, where key Houthi-held ports and oil infrastructure are located. The Coalition has not confirmed strikes there; Reuters separately reported the Coalition's evacuation order for the Sanaa oil facility ahead of an operation.

items.title: Yemeni officials urge Sanaa residents to stay away from sites likely to be targeted; Houthis accused of using civilians as human shields
items.body: An adviser to Yemen's prime minister said the Houthis store weapons in civilian sites and that Coalition warnings before striking facilities meet the rules of engagement and international humanitarian law. Earlier, an adviser to Yemen's interior minister told Sanaa residents to keep away from facilities that could be targeted.

items.title: Yemeni Armed Forces: 2,200 precision strikes in operation “Dawn of Yemen”; about 1,200 Houthi fighters neutralised (their estimate)
items.body: The Yemeni government forces' spokesperson said 2,200 precision strikes were carried out on the eastern and southern fronts under operation “Dawn of Yemen”, with strikes in Taiz hitting Houthi columns. Their preliminary field estimate is about 1,200 Houthi fighters neutralised and more than 440 vehicles destroyed or disabled; these figures are the Yemeni forces' own and are not independently verified.

items.title: Houthi spokesman says fighters are confronting Saudi-backed forces in Sanaa; Al Arabiya reports airstrikes on al-Sabaha oil terminal
items.body: Al Jazeera quoted a Houthi spokesman as saying their fighters were confronting Saudi-backed forces in Sanaa, shortly after explosions were reported there. Arab News, citing Al Arabiya TV, said airstrikes targeted the Houthi-held al-Sabaha oil terminal, the site named in the Coalition's 3:22 PM evacuation warning. The Coalition had not confirmed a strike by the 6:18 PM check.

items.title: Egypt's foreign minister: Cairo ready to give Saudi Arabia any support, including possible military assistance
items.body: Egyptian Foreign Minister Badr Abdelatty said Cairo is prepared to provide Saudi Arabia with any form of support, including potential military assistance, as the Kingdom faces intensified Houthi attacks.

items.title: Al Jazeera: explosions heard in Sanaa; Houthi-affiliated media report strikes on an oil facility
items.body: An Al Jazeera correspondent reported hearing explosions in Houthi-controlled Sanaa, and Houthi-affiliated media said Saudi-backed forces struck an oil facility. The Coalition has not confirmed any strike; this is a single-outlet report plus a Houthi media claim.

items.title: Turkish President Erdoğan calls the Crown Prince, condemns the Houthi attacks and offers condolences
items.body: In a phone call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, President Erdoğan condemned the Houthi attacks on the Kingdom, offered condolences for those killed and wished the injured a quick recovery. He affirmed Türkiye's full support for the Kingdom's security.

items.title: German Chancellor Merz calls the Crown Prince and condemns the Houthi terrorist attacks on the Kingdom
items.body: Chancellor Friedrich Merz condemned the Houthi terrorist attacks targeting the Kingdom's security and stability in a call with the Crown Prince, and affirmed Germany's support and solidarity.

items.title: Lebanese President calls the Crown Prince and condemns the attacks targeting the Kingdom
items.body: Lebanon's president condemned the attacks targeting the Kingdom in a call with the Crown Prince and affirmed Lebanon's solidarity against anything that threatens its security, sovereignty and territorial integrity.

items.title: Coalition: evacuation warning for civilians at Yemen Oil Company / central al-Sabaha station in Sanaa
items.body: The Coalition Joint Forces Command asked civilians to evacuate the Yemen Oil Company / central al-Sabaha station site in Sanaa for their safety, with a map of the location. SPA and Al Ekhbariya carried the same warning. This is a Coalition warning in Yemen, not a strike on Saudi territory.

items.title: Kuwait interior minister: Kuwait stands with Saudi Arabia against Houthi attacks
items.body: Kuwait's First Deputy Prime Minister and Interior Minister Sheikh Fahad Al-Yousef Al-Sabah said Kuwait stands fully with the Kingdom against what it is facing from Houthi attacks.

items.title: Al Ekhbariya from Aden: Yemeni forces advance west of Taiz, al-Jawf and Marib; Houthi cells disrupted
items.body: Al Ekhbariya's Aden correspondent reported field advances by armed forces west of Taiz, al-Jawf and Marib; security moves in Lahj and Aden to foil Houthi plots; cells linked to the Houthis arrested in Aden, Lahj and Abyan; airstrikes on Houthi reinforcements heading to front lines.

items.title: Coalition: 3 drones intercepted and destroyed north of Riyadh
items.body: The Coalition spokesman confirmed interception and destruction of three unmanned aerial vehicles north of Riyadh. SPA and Al Ekhbariya carried the same statement.

items.title: SPA: Coalition intercepted and destroyed 3 drones north of Riyadh
items.body: Saudi Press Agency reports the Coalition intercepted and destroyed three drones north of Riyadh.

items.title: SPA: Tunisia condemns repeated attacks on vital facilities and infrastructure in Saudi Arabia
items.body: Saudi Press Agency (English) reports that Tunisia condemned the repeated attacks on vital facilities and infrastructure in Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Reuters/AP: Riyadh airport closure extended to 12:00 AM Sunday 18 Oct (NOTAM); Saudis probe how air defences failed
items.body: GACA said operations at King Khalid International Airport are suspended to complete safety and operational-readiness checks; a NOTAM keeps it closed until 12:00 AM Sunday 18 Oct (Riyadh time). Two regional officials told AP that Saudi Arabia is investigating why air defences failed to stop the drone, cruise and ballistic missile barrage on the airport. Lufthansa Group has cancelled Riyadh flights until 16 Oct and Air France-KLM until the end of October.

items.title: SPA: Denmark strongly condemns Houthi attacks on the Kingdom’s airports
items.body: Saudi Press Agency reports that Denmark strongly condemned the Houthi attacks on airports in the Kingdom.

items.title: SPA: UAE Foreign Minister calls Saudi Foreign Minister, condemns Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport and affirms full solidarity
items.body: His Highness the Foreign Minister received a phone call from the UAE Foreign Minister, who expressed the UAE’s condemnation of the Houthi militia attacks on King Khalid International Airport and affirmed his country’s full solidarity with the Kingdom and support for everything that preserves its security and stability. The two ministers also discussed recent developments and their repercussions.

items.title: SPA: Foreign Minister receives a call from Malaysia’s foreign minister condemning attacks on civilians in the Kingdom; Malaysia affirms solidarity and support for measures to protect sovereignty, security and residents
items.body: His Highness the Foreign Minister received a phone call from Malaysia’s Foreign Minister, who affirmed his country’s condemnation of the attacks that targeted civilians in the Kingdom, Malaysia’s solidarity with the Kingdom, and support for all measures it takes to safeguard its sovereignty, security and stability and to protect its citizens and residents; other issues were also reviewed.

items.title: Saudi MOFA: Crown Prince receives a call from the King of Jordan condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.body: 🇸🇦📞🇯🇴 | HRH the Crown Prince receives a call from the King of Jordan condemning Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Trump says the Houthis are “misbehaving very badly” over attacks on Saudi airports, without outlining a US response
items.body: US President Donald Trump criticised the Iran-backed Houthis over repeated attacks on Saudi Arabia’s airports and civilian infrastructure, saying the group is “misbehaving very badly.” Arab News noted he did not outline any specific US response.

items.title: Bloomberg: Egypt says it is ready to offer any kind of support to Saudi Arabia against the Houthis
items.body: Bloomberg reported that Egypt said it is ready to offer any kind of support to Saudi Arabia in its fight with the Houthis in Yemen. The original Egyptian government statement has not been checked directly.

items.title: King Khalid airport tells a passenger asking whether the airport is still closed to follow official authorities and contact their airline
items.body: Replying to a passenger with a flight on 15 October who asked whether the airport is still closed, the official King Khalid International Airport account said that for the latest airspace updates passengers should follow the competent official authorities and contact the airline they booked with. It gave no reopening date.

items.title: Reuters: authorities extend Riyadh airport closure until 17 October as airlines scrap flights
items.body: Reuters reported that authorities have extended the closure of Riyadh's international airport until 17 October, and that airlines scrapped flights after continuing Houthi attacks emptied the skies over the capital. This matches the NOTAM keeping the aerodrome unavailable until 12:00 AM Sunday 18 October.

items.title: AFP: blasts over Riyadh again Monday night; coalition says it intercepted a Houthi missile
items.body: AFP reported that blasts were heard over Riyadh again on Monday night after lethal weekend strikes on Riyadh's airport. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted a Houthi missile. AFP also noted Houthi warnings to the US of a "painful response" if it enters the conflict.

items.title: Reuters: Saudi-led coalition destroyed Houthi ballistic missile fired toward Riyadh
items.body: Reuters reported that the Saudi-led coalition said it destroyed a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward Riyadh, matching coalition/SPA intercept statements from Monday night.

items.title: Anadolu: several Arab airlines suspend or cancel flights to Riyadh after deadly Houthi attacks
items.body: Anadolu reported that several Arab airlines have suspended or cancelled flights to Riyadh after deadly Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport. It restated Saturday's toll of 13 killed and more than 300 injured, plus a further Sunday strike that killed 1 and injured over 10.

items.title: SPA: NCM forecasts thunderstorms and flash floods across much of the Kingdom, including Riyadh and Eastern Province
items.body: Saudi Press Agency relayed an NCM forecast of moderate to heavy thunderstorms with hail and active winds over Jazan, Asir, Al-Baha and Makkah, lighter to moderate over Najran, Medina, Hail, Tabuk, Al-Jouf, Northern Borders, Riyadh and the Eastern Province, with fog in parts.

items.title: ABS-CBN: Philippine Airlines suspends Riyadh flights until 29 November
items.body: ABS-CBN News reported that Philippine Airlines has suspended its flights to and from Riyadh until 29 November 2026, citing the security situation at King Khalid International Airport. The airline's own notice has not been checked directly.

items.title: Houthis claim ballistic missile at King Khalid airport and drone at Khamis Mushait base on Monday evening
items.body: Houthi spokesman Yahya Sarea claimed a ballistic missile attack on King Khalid International Airport and a drone attack on the Khamis Mushait air base on Monday evening. The coalition said the missile fired toward Riyadh was intercepted and destroyed. Some OSINT accounts say it hit inside the airport perimeter; that is unconfirmed and conflicts with the official statement.

items.title: Family of a young Jordanian man killed in the King Khalid airport attack speak to Al Ekhbariya
items.body: Al Ekhbariya aired interviews with the father and a cousin of a young Jordanian man who died in the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport. His father said he lost his son to the brutal attack on innocent people, and his cousin called on countries to stand up to attacks targeting Arab states.

items.title: Khaleej Times: Etihad cancels all Abu Dhabi–Riyadh flights until 19 Oct; Jeddah and Dammam until 14 Oct
items.body: Etihad cancelled all Abu Dhabi–Riyadh flights until 19 Oct amid the Riyadh airport closure, and Abu Dhabi–Jeddah and Abu Dhabi–Dammam until 14 Oct, citing regional disruption.

items.title: Media Minister: Saudi Arabia stands strong through national unity and puts people at the heart of development
items.body: SPA reported the Media Minister saying Saudi Arabia stands strong through national unity and keeps people at the heart of development.

items.title: Kazakhstan condemns Houthi militia attacks on civilian infrastructure facilities in the Kingdom
items.body: Kazakhstan condemns Houthi militia attacks on civilian infrastructure facilities in the Kingdom

items.title: 176 ministers, scholars, muftis and Islamic leaders from more than 70 countries condemn the Houthi attacks and affirm solidarity with the Kingdom
items.body: 176 ministers, scholars, muftis and Islamic leaders from more than 70 countries condemn the Houthi attacks and affirm solidarity with the Kingdom

items.title: Grand Mufti: Houthi targeting of the holy sites and pilgrims to the Two Holy Mosques is a grave crime
items.body: Al Ekhbariya's roundup of Monday 12 October quoted the Kingdom's Grand Mufti as saying the Houthi militia's targeting of the holy sites and of pilgrims to the Two Holy Mosques is a grave crime with dire consequences. The roundup also restated the King of Jordan's call to the Crown Prince condemning the attacks and the destruction of three Houthi ballistic missiles on Monday.

items.title: Bloomberg: barrage of drone and missile attacks raises pressure on Washington to help Saudi Arabia against the Houthis
items.body: Bloomberg reported that the barrage of drone and missile attacks on Saudi Arabia has intensified pressure on Washington to step up efforts to help its ally against the Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen. This is analysis, not an official US statement.

items.title: Al-Azhar and the Arab Red Crescent body condemn the attack on King Khalid International Airport
items.body: Saudi Press Agency reported that Al-Azhar strongly condemned the attack on King Khalid International Airport. The Arab Red Crescent and Red Cross Organization (ARCO) said attacks on Saudi civilian facilities and the intimidation of civilians breach international conventions.

items.title: UN Secretary-General strongly condemns repeated Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport
items.source: Al Arabiya English (@AlArabiya_Eng), citing UN spokesman Stephane Dujarric
items.body: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres strongly condemned the repeated Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh and other civilian infrastructure across Saudi Arabia, his spokesman said. Saudi Press Agency separately reported that the UN human rights chief condemned the attacks on airports in the Kingdom.

items.title: Coalition: two Houthi ballistic missiles fired toward Khamis Mushait intercepted and destroyed
items.body: The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed two ballistic missiles launched by the Houthis toward Khamis Mushait in southwestern Saudi Arabia. Civil Defense announced the danger had passed in Khamis Mushait. No damage or casualties were reported.

items.title: OPEC+ Declaration of Cooperation energy ministers meet in Riyadh on the sidelines of the IEF and World Petroleum Congress
items.body: Energy and oil ministers of the countries in the OPEC+ Declaration of Cooperation held a meeting in Riyadh on the sidelines of the 17th IEF Ministerial Meeting and the 25th WPC Energy Congress. No output decision was reported in the post.

items.title: Civil Defense: filming or sharing information about interceptions and impact sites exposes people to legal liability
items.body: Civil Defense, citing the Interior Ministry, warned that filming, publishing or sharing information about missile and drone interceptions and where debris falls can lead to legal action.

items.title: Energy Minister: East-West pipeline is a strategic asset that gives Saudi crude an alternative route to world markets via the Red Sea
items.body: Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman said the East-West pipeline links eastern oil production centres to the Red Sea and provides an alternative route to global markets when shipping faces restrictions. He said the Kingdom's real resilience lies in its people's ability to maintain and repair facilities and keep supplies flowing under pressure.

items.title: King Khalid airport tells passengers to check flight status with their airline
items.body: Replying to passengers, the airport asked people to contact their airline to confirm flight status and get updates. At 8:26 PM it said cars in its car parks can be collected once operations resume, confirming operations are still suspended.

items.title: Muslim World League receives messages from across the Muslim world condemning the Houthi attacks on the Kingdom
items.body: SPA reports the Muslim World League has received cables and letters from across the Islamic world condemning the Houthi terrorist attacks on Saudi Arabia.

items.title: Arab News: US embassy says American citizens were detained for filming recent events in Saudi Arabia
items.body: Arab News reports the US embassy in Riyadh said American citizens had been detained for filming recent events. Saudi authorities have warned that filming or sharing information about missile and drone interceptions carries legal liability.

items.title: Some people injured in the Houthi attack on King Khalid airport have recovered and left hospital
items.body: Al Ekhbariya's correspondent said a number of people injured in the Houthi attack on King Khalid International Airport have recovered and left hospital. Some of the injured were transit passengers on their way to perform Umrah, and the leadership's directions include bringing relatives of the injured from abroad.

items.title: Coalition: Houthi ballistic missile fired toward Riyadh intercepted and destroyed; Civil Defense says the danger has passed
items.source: Coalition spokesman (@CJFCSpox) / SPA / Saudi Civil Defense
items.body: The coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a ballistic missile launched by the Houthis toward Riyadh, after the 9:00 PM early-warning alert. Civil Defense announced at 9:11 PM that the danger had passed in Riyadh city and warned that filming or sharing information about interceptions or impact sites exposes people to legal liability. No damage or casualties have been reported.

items.title: Civil Defense issues early-warning alert for Riyadh city over a potential danger
items.body: Saudi Civil Defense said the National Early Warning Platform issued an emergency alert in Riyadh city warning of a potential danger. The coalition then said it intercepted a Houthi ballistic missile fired toward Riyadh, and Civil Defense declared the danger over at 9:11 PM.

items.title: Ministers, scholars and muftis from more than 70 countries condemn Houthi attacks on the Two Holy Mosques, airports and civilian sites
items.body: SPA reports that ministers, scholars and muftis from more than 70 countries condemned and denounced the Houthi militia's targeting of the Two Holy Mosques, airports and civilian facilities in the Kingdom.

items.title: Leadership directs free full medical care for people injured in the Houthi attack on King Khalid airport
items.body: Al Ekhbariya reports from a Riyadh hospital that leadership directed free full medical care for those injured in the Houthi attacks on King Khalid International Airport, with health teams continuing close follow-up.

items.title: Crown Prince receives call from King of Jordan condemning the Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia
items.body: SPA reports that Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman received a phone call from King Abdullah II of Jordan, who condemned the Houthi attacks on the Kingdom.

strikes.title: Escalation pattern: Houthi strikes on KSA by target type
strikes.so_what: The campaign has climbed an escalation ladder: from military targets to economic targets (Aramco, Yanbu), then to symbolic targets (the Madinah power station serving the Prophet’s Mosque), and now to civilian aviation and the capital. King Khalid International Airport has been hit or targeted on 19 Sep, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 11 Oct; the 10–11 Oct strikes closed it indefinitely. On the evening of 11 Oct GACA confirmed a further attack on Dammam’s King Fahd International Airport. Each rung raises the reputational cost to the Kingdom more than the military cost.

items.detail: The UK issued an alert and updated travel advice on 6 Oct, after a US Mission alert on 5 Oct.

items.detail: GCC and Arab leaders and the UN Secretary-General condemned the deadly attacks on Saudi airports.

airports_rule: Which pill is shown: Riyadh (RUH) and Dammam (DMM) use the level in the hourly report feed, with the automatic check as a small note. Other airports use KSA Bot's editor level (blocks/airports.json) while its check is under 3 hours old; if the check is older, or has no dated time, the automatic check becomes the pill with a note 'Last editor check: ...'. Automatic check from the live Flightradar24 boards, 3-hour lookback; an official or NOTAM closure overrides it. HALTED: 0 takeoffs/landings for 45+ minutes while 2 or more flights scheduled in that window did not operate (cancelled, diverted, or 60+ minutes past schedule with no actual time); at small airports (under 60 flights a day) it needs 3+ flights not operated AND 90+ minutes with 0 movements. QUIET (grey): 0 movements but not enough flights due, e.g. an overnight lull or night closure; the next scheduled flight is shown. DISRUPTED: 15%+ of today's flights cancelled, any diversion today, a halt in the last 6 hours, or a night/partial NOTAM restriction. NORMAL: none of these. NO DATA: the board returned no rows. FR24 'Unknown' flights with no actual time count as due only once 60+ minutes overdue. DATA GAP: a gap where flights scheduled in it show Landed/Departed without times, or later show actual times on both sides, is a Flightradar24 data gap, not a halt.
